description: Acquiring or releasing a mutex (k_mutex_lock/unlock) or I2C bus lock inside an ISR callback causes thread scheduling corruption.
Functions marked @funcprops \sleep yield threads and cannot be called inside an interrupt handler.
Calling an API inside an ISR context that is not explicitly annotated as @funcprops \isr_ok.
Acquiring or releasing mutexes during early PRE_KERNEL_1 / PRE_KERNEL_2 boot hooks before the kernel thread scheduler is online.
Calling un-annotated or sleeping functions during early boot initialization hooks before thread scheduling is active.
Performing synchronous I2C transactions (i2c_read/write/transceive) inside an ISR stalls interrupt processing for milliseconds due to clock stretching.
Calling thread yielding or sleeping functions while holding an IRQ lock, spinlock, or scheduler lock causes deadlock.
